active_storylines.storyline_label: Nvidia GTC Taipei — Vera Rubin volume production + RTX Spark Superchip in Microsoft Surface Laptop Ultra
active_storylines.last_state_change_summary: Jensen Huang's GTC Taipei 2026 keynote at Computex Monday June 1 shipped production artifacts rather than a roadmap. Vera Rubin entered volume production: the third-gen MGX rack-scale platform pairs Rubin GPUs with the 88-core Vera Olympus CPU, NVLink 6 Switch, ConnectX-9 SuperNIC, BlueField-4 STX DPU (and Groq 3 LPU per the news section), NVL72 rack carrying 72 Rubin GPUs + 36 Vera CPUs; Nvidia claims one-fourth the GPU count of Grace Blackwell for equivalent MoE training and 10x inference throughput at one-tenth per-token cost, first systems shipping fall 2026 from Dell, HPE, Supermicro, Lenovo across 350+ supply-chain partners in 30 countries. The long-rumored N1X arrived as the RTX Spark Superchip — 20 Arm CPU cores co-designed with MediaTek + Blackwell GPU with 6,144 CUDA cores + 128GB unified LPDDR5X on TSMC 3nm, 1 petaflop FP4, runs 120B-parameter LLMs at 1M-token context locally. Microsoft simultaneously launched the Surface Laptop Ultra (15-inch mini-LED PixelSense Ultra, 128GB unified memory, Windows on Arm) as the first RTX Spark device, with ASUS, Dell, HP, Lenovo, MSI follow-ons fall 2026 (Acer/Gigabyte trailing). DGX Station for Windows on the GB300 Grace Blackwell Ultra Desktop Superchip delivers 20 petaflops FP4 at up to 748GB memory, Q4 2026 from Dell, HP, ASUSTeK, MSI, Supermicro.

active_storylines.storyline_label: Commerce OIG names four NIST failures behind 27,000-CVE NVD backlog + Microsoft Defender EPSS exposure score
active_storylines.last_state_change_summary: A US Department of Commerce Office of Inspector General report published Monday June 1 details how NIST failed to manage the National Vulnerability Database through the contract gap from February 2024 (enrichment-contractor support ended) to November 2024 (replacement secured), letting the backlog of unprocessed vulnerabilities balloon past 27,000 by end-2025 against projected 2026 CVE volume above 60,000 — a near tenfold increase from a decade ago. OIG names four problems: no formal NVD strategy, duplicate severity scoring on 80% of submissions already carrying scores, redundant CISA/NIST enrichment without coordination, and stakeholder updates lagging operational reality; NIST has until July 25, 2026 to submit a formal action plan. Same day, Microsoft moved Defender Vulnerability Management's exposure score (now public preview) off raw CVSS dependence, blending EPSS exploit-likelihood signals, internet-facing status, and asset criticality into a single representative score answering 'where to remediate first?' rather than 'how severe is the CVE?' — directly addressing the prioritization gap the OIG says the federal pipeline left unfilled.

active_storylines.storyline_label: Anthropic Claude containment architecture published (gVisor + Seatbelt/Bubblewrap + per-OS VMs)
active_storylines.last_state_change_summary: Anthropic engineering blog published 'How we contain Claude across products' Saturday May 30, walking through the three-tier reference design: gVisor + seccomp on isolated infra for Claude.ai (ephemeral per-session FS), OS-native sandboxes for Claude Code (Seatbelt macOS, Bubblewrap Linux, 84% permission-prompt reduction via model-classifier delegation), guest VMs for Claude Cowork on Apple Virtualization Framework macOS + HCS Windows with host-held credentials + read-only/read-write/read-write-no-delete file mount modes. Argument: 'the software you build yourself is often the weakest' — mature hypervisors and container runtimes outperform custom security wrappers. Simon Willison amplified Saturday evening and demonstrated by getting Opus 4.8 (Claude Code for web) to refactor Datasette Lite from Web Workers to service workers — Python ASGI server-side in browser via Pyodide + working FastCGI demo + Datasette 1.0a31. NOTE: structurally adjacent to Nvidia OpenShell (June 1) and Microsoft Windows Agent Framework (Build June 2-3) — three OS-sandbox agent-runtime postures now in market within one week.
